decisions: monthKeyOf IS NOT THE BUG AND WAS NOT TOUCHED. Its own comment in lib/commission.ts says it buckets an ISO timestamp by the UTC instant deliberately, so payroll grouping is deterministic across machines. The bug was using a BUCKETING helper to ask a CLOCK question - monthKeyOf(new Date().toISOString()). currentMonthKey() answers the clock question; monthKeyOf keeps bucketing stored timestamps. Two different questions that happen to agree for 21 hours a day.

THE COLUMN TYPE ON THE OTHER SIDE DECIDED HOW CLEAN EACH FIX WAS, so the types were checked rather than assumed: trips.trip_date and customer_topups.topup_date are DATE (already a local calendar month, so both sides now align exactly), while trips.delivered_at is TIMESTAMPTZ (bucketed by UTC by design). BreakdownReport and FinanceTab touch only DATE columns; CustomersTab touches both.

A STATED RESIDUAL BEATS A SILENT ONE. CustomersTab keeps a known three-hour gap on the 1st for its two delivered_at figures. It is strictly better than the old behaviour (the whole tab showed the wrong month) but it is not zero, so it is written into the code at the declaration rather than left for someone to rediscover as a fresh bug.

currentMonthKey LIVES IN lib/utils.ts, BESIDE todayKey() - it is a clock helper, not commission logic. It was promoted out of lib/commission-rows.ts the moment a second consumer appeared; three non-commission surfaces read it now, and importing that from a commission module would have been the wrong dependency. Same precedent as daysAgoKey being promoted in 22aad18. commission-rows RE-EXPORTS it so its four write sites are unaffected and there is exactly ONE definition.

A MODULE-LEVEL CONST THAT READS THE CLOCK IS A BUG, NOT A CACHE. The original CURRENT_MONTH_KEY was computed once at module load and never rolled over - stale for the lifetime of a session or process. The UTC skew was the smaller half. Anything answering 'what is now' must be called, not captured.

MONTH_KEY IS LOAD-BEARING ON THE WRITE PATH. v_commissions_monthly attributes specials, adjustments AND the bonus by exact string match, and v_driver_payslip_basis reads through it. The 'month_key is kept only as a human label' comment on setCommissionBonus describes that upsert's CONFLICT TARGET (driver_id alone) and is not a statement about the views.

NO NEW DATE HELPERS IN THE WHOLE SWEEP. Everything routes through todayKey / daysAgoKey / currentMonthKey in lib/utils.ts. today+7 is daysAgoKey(-7) - the existing helper's own arithmetic - proven under TZ=Asia/Riyadh across month and year rollovers.

MIGRATIONS ARE COMMITTED THE MOMENT THE APPLY IS CONFIRMED (the db-reset rule), and the apply is VERIFIED rather than taken on report. 0120's anon check was the one that mattered: default privileges re-grant anon on every newly created relation and a REVOKE does not survive a DROP. It held - 40 views, 40 invoker, 0 anon-readable.
